samples.identification: Entrypoint SDK darwin-arm64 0.2.1: official FRP client plus caller-configured connector
samples.marker_line: Entrypoint SDK: Configured FRP/VPN; fix X.509 field classification
behaviors: Manifest has no install hook, executable JS entrypoint or declared dependencies. It ships two arm64 Mach-O executables.
Bundled frpc SHA-256 7aaaba058dbeeedc86be876c44912c4f33756ab3e6e7a085f8d7af7814a073c1 equals the separately fetched official FRP 0.71.1 darwin-arm64 release.

Recovered connector Go pclntab names and ARM64 main disassembly: main.main 0x100798ae0 dispatches tunnel/vpn/rebundle/version; main.tunnel 0x100798e60 reads ENTRYPOINT_CONNECT then DecodeBundle, connector.New and Connector.Run. Missing configuration errors out.

Connector.Run 0x100793650 creates temporary configuration/CA files, sets mode 0700, configures a loopback admin port and random password. runFrpc 0x100795380 calls exec.Command at 0x1007953d0 with configured executable and [-c, cfgPath], passes token environment, relays stdout, waits/restarts; parent pipe closes/drain/stop end it. Cleanup removes its temporary config directory.

VPN path main.vpn 0x100799ab0 reads caller ENTRYPOINT_VPN and exposes/forwards explicitly configured ports. RunVPN 0x100796a10 invokes tsnet.Server.Up at 0x100796c18 then accepts/dials and copies peer TCP streams. Durable VPN state stores node identity, not an autorun registration.

Retrieved source at embedded VCS revision 6e10b79410d9702e6068dd7de665b9d97b9bd067 matches these paths and application function inventory. Caller SDK 0.2.1 separately fetched: tunnel(opts) explicitly spawns connector with caller bundle/upstream; importing/installing does not launch a tunnel.

Generic DoH, AWS metadata, process APIs, crypto and frontend JS strings originate in the linked Tailscale/FRP libraries; their accurate capability/reference detections remain. No hidden endpoint or secret-acquisition-to-send path was found in the program entry/control paths.
limitations_and_source_label: No operator deployment record, caller bundle or authorization context. A configured FRP/VPN can serve unauthorized access, but the artifact alone supplies no malicious configuration. No independent connector reproducible-build hash comparison; source and disassembly correspondence is narrower evidence.

GHSA/OSV repeat a generic compromise notice without a sample-specific execution account. Legitimate bundled FRP and remote-access capability plausibly explain the source label, but the precise flagging trigger is unknown.

samples.marker_line: thornqueue: Campaign remote-script loader; add bound bootstrap launch
behaviors: Exact original wheel recovered using forager --all-wheels; SHA-256 matches the submitted wheel. Only one release wheel was returned. METADATA agrees with name/version; no dependencies or entrypoint hook.

Full source and bootstrap inspected: import creates fixed dot-prefixed temp workspace only. run requires a caller URL. _fetch retries urllib.urlopen, reads its body, writes job.py and returns that path.
run writes keyword arguments to manifest.json and embedded _BOOTSTRAP to boot.py, then subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, boot, script, manifest]); waits and returns exit status.

Child bootstrap creates importlib spec from sys.argv[1], creates module namespace, exec_module executes the fetched file, then calls mod.run(**json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))). Separate process is not a sandbox: inherited privileges/environment; no signature/digest policy, no cleanup of jobs, no automatic persistence registration.

The oddly vertical initial docstring and repeated no-evaluation-in-this-process prose change presentation, not the execution path. There is no hidden encoded stage beyond the visible bootstrap string. Example URL is reserved .example and not a live payload endpoint.

Primary researcher attributes thornqueue to coordinated 2026-10-voice-synthesis-profiles loaders; recovered slatejob original independently corroborates near-identical staging/bootstrap architecture. That provenance plus the verified loader path tips likely-malicious judgement. Source explicitly says campaign usage is unknown.
limitations_and_source_label: No caller, real payload URL, delivered payload, victim target, secret theft, attacker command, evasion gate or persistence found in the available bytes.

Hostile-trait goal remains unmet: all observed primitives and the newly bound bootstrap launch also serve legitimate runners. Campaign attribution is contextual evidence outside these bytes, not a generalizable hostile static matcher. No duplicate, package-name conviction or invented theft/C2 rule was added. Classifier remains benign: this is a context-driven classifier disagreement, not resolved by the increased raw probability.

samples.marker_line: Easemon redirect: Portal navigation; no payload or theft in HTML
behaviors: All 103 bytes are one script assigning an absolute HTTPS URL to location. No form, credential read, download operation, eval, encoded stage, or persistence in the original HTML.

The double hash starts a URL fragment. The HTTP request goes to /index.php; /index.php?m=device&a=download_android_html is fragment text for the authenticated portal route, not an automatic Android download in these bytes.
Fetched /index.php currently navigates to Easemon Cloud login. Also fetched the explicit Android route without fragment; it is authentication-gated and returns login navigation.

Login uses same-origin authentication/recovery endpoints. Retrieved jQuery, language dictionary, Cloudflare telemetry, unbundled MD5/login and lost-password scripts. Reviewed relevant handlers: password hashing, same-origin POSTs, result-directed navigation and Google sign-in integration. No replacement credential collector or delivered Android payload found.

PageSpeed combined script URL returned HTTP 200 through forager but could not be saved because its filename exceeds filesystem length; direct urllib fallback was HTTP 403. Its available unbundled md5/lost-password constituents were fetched and reviewed instead. Google sign-in SDK request was HTTP 403. This limits dependency completeness; no APK was recovered or synthesized.
limitations_and_source_label: Easemon is a monitoring/stalkerware-associated product; its own website promotes stealth monitoring and threat research has classified variants as spyware. Association plausibly explains the hostile source label.

A shortcut to an operator portal does not itself implement surveillance or prove unauthorized installation. Account/consent, prior server content and the authenticated Android payload are unavailable. Verdict applies to submitted HTML; current landing page does not establish historical safety.
